title: Evidence and Hearing Assistance: Exhibits, Subpoenas and Interpreters in Unemployment Insurance Appeals
content:
Documentary exhibits in Unemployment Insurance Appeals must be received no later than the exhibit deadline business days before the hearing, counted backward in business days from the hearing date; an exhibit received later is recorded as late and admitted only with good cause. Each party sends its exhibits to the appeals office and to every other party. A subpoena for a witness or document must be requested no later than the subpoena business days before the hearing. An interpreter is provided free of charge in the requested language, and a request is recorded once per party and language. Exhibits and interpreter requests are not taken on a Board of Review appeal, which is decided on the lower-authority record and written argument.

## Exhibits

- **Deadline.** The docket's exhibit deadline is a number of business days before the hearing, counted backward from the hearing date.
- **Status on receipt.** Each exhibit received is recorded with its kind, the party that submitted it and the date received, and is marked as having met the deadline or as late.
- **Late exhibits.** A late exhibit is admitted only with good cause.
- **Service.** A party sends each exhibit both to the appeals office and to every other party.

*Boundary case (hypothetical hearing date and a hypothetical deadline of two business days; no state holiday in the span):* for a hearing on Thursday 16 April 2026 the exhibit deadline falls on Tuesday 14 April. An exhibit received on 14 April met the deadline; one received on Wednesday 15 April is recorded as late and is admitted only with good cause.

## Subpoenas

A subpoena for a witness or for a document must be requested no later than the docket's subpoena lead, counted in business days before the hearing.

## Interpreters

| Point | Rule |
|---|---|
| Cost | free of charge |
| Language | the language requested |
| Recording | one request per party per language; the same party asking again for the same language is the same request, while a second language, or another party, is a separate request |

## Board of Review

On a Board of Review appeal no exhibits and no interpreter requests are taken: the Board decides on the lower-authority record and written argument.
